Rashi on Pesachim 118a:11:1.hebrew: קשין נקביו של אדם - כשהוא עצור, כיום המיתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 118a:11:1.english: A person's orifices are difficult - When he is constipated, [they are] like the day of death.

Rashi on Pesachim 118a:1:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: רביעי גומר עליו את ההלל, ואומר עליו הלל הגדול:
Rashi on Pesachim 118a:1:1.english: We read [the text as follows]: [With regard to the] fourth [cup], one completes Hallel over it and recites the Great Hallel over it.

Rashi on Pesachim 118a:3:1.hebrew: שהקדוש ברוך הוא יושב ברומו של עולם כו' - דכתיב: "הודו לאל השמים", "נותן לחם לכל בשר", והיינו דבר גדול:
Rashi on Pesachim 118a:3:1.english: That the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits in the heights of the universe, etc. - For it is written: "Give thanks to the God of heaven," [and] "Who gives food to all flesh" — and this is a great thing.

Rashi on Pesachim 118a:5:1.english: A wealthy [person] with his ox - [He] causes him a financial loss, [and it atones] for his body.

Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:1:1.hebrew: מאי ברכת השיר רב יהודה אמר יהללוך - וקמ"ל דאפילו במקום שלא נהגו לברך אחריו, בלילי פסח צריך לברך, דאי נהגו — פשיטא. א"נ, דאפילו במקום שנהגו, ה"א דוקא בימים, אבל בלילה אין צריך לברך — קא משמע לן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:1:1.english: "What is the blessing of the song? Rav Yehuda said: 'They shall praise You'" - And [this] teaches us that even in a place where they are not accustomed to recite a blessing after [Hallel], on the nights of Passover one must recite the blessing, for if they were accustomed [to do so], it would be obvious. Alternatively, even in a place where they are accustomed [to do so], I would have thought [that this applies] specifically during the days, whereas at night one does not need to recite the blessing; [therefore, the Gemara] teaches us [that one must].

Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:1:2.hebrew: רבי יוחנן אמר נשמת כל חי - נראה ה"פ: אף נשמת כל חי אחר יהללוך, דאי לא תימא הכי — אנן כמאן עבדינן? וקורא "נשמת כל חי" "ברכת השיר", לפי שבשבתות אומרים אותו אחר פסוקי דזמרה. ורבינו חיים כהן לא היה חותם ב"יהללוך", כי אם ב"נשמת" לבדו, משום דלישנא ד"ברכת השיר" משמע חדא ברכה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:1:2.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Nishmat Kol Chai ["The breath of all living"] - It seems that its explanation is: [one recites] Nishmat Kol Chai as well, after Yehallelukha, for if you do not say so, in accordance with whom do we act? And [Rabbi Yoḥanan] calls Nishmat Kol Chai "the blessing of the song" because on Shabbatot we recite it after pesukei dezimra. However, Rabbeinu Chaim Kohen would not conclude with Yehallelukha, but rather with Nishmat alone, because the wording "the blessing of the song" implies a single blessing.

Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:2:1.hebrew: מהודו עד על נהרות בבל - וכן אנו עושים; ו"רננו צדיקים בה'" אינו מן המזמור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 118a:2:1.english: From "Give thanks" until "By the rivers of Babylon" - And so we do; and "Rejoice, O righteous, in the Lord" is not part of the psalm.
